english.title: Damage / destroy nest of non-Schedule 1 wild bird
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), intentionally damaged or destroyed

(A)_[the nest of a wild bird,]_
(B)_[the nests of wild birds,]_
(C)_[**(..SPECIFY..) nests of wild birds,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY BIRD(S)..), while

(D)_[it was]_
(E)_[they were]_

in use or being built
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(1)(b) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) See Sections 2 and Section 4 for exceptions.
(ii) See Sections 1(6) and 27 for meaning of "wild bird".
(iii) See Section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
(iv) See Section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one nest is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each nest (Section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
